title: SageSched: Efficient LLM Scheduling Confronting Demand Uncertainty and Hybridity
claim: Real workloads show highly variable output lengths per request and divergent compute-versus-memory demands across request types.
layout: 2 panels side by side, left-to-right, violin plot beside hexbin scatter
description: Two side-by-side empirical plots with captions (a) and (b). Panel (a) is a violin plot with box overlays. The x-axis is Request ID, 1 to 10, and the y-axis is normalized output length with a broken axis. Each of ten prompts shows a wide, uneven distribution of output lengths over 100 runs. Blue violins, white interquartile boxes, orange medians and magenta min-max lines are drawn against a dotted line at 1.0. Panel (b) is a hexbin scatter of execution time in seconds against peak memory usage in GB for three datasets: Sharegpt in blue, Alpaca in orange and Write in green. Alpaca is memory-heavy but fast. Write is slow with low memory. Sharegpt is scattered, with outliers. The two spread-out clouds of points draw the eye first.
caption: Empirical evidences on the uncertainty and hybridity characteristics of LLM inferences' resource demands.
abstract: Efficient LLM inference scheduling is crucial for user experience. However, LLM inferences exhibit remarkable demand uncertainty (with unknown output length beforehand) and hybridity (being both compute and memory intensive). Existing LLM schedulers rely on simple heuristics or focus purely on compute resource, suffering suboptimal performance. In this work, we propose SageSched, an efficient LLM scheduler that properly handles demand uncertainty and hybridity of inference workloads. SageSched combines prompt contents with the past inference results to predict output-length distribution in a light-weight and also accurate manner. Meanwhile, it models the true service cost of an inference request with both compute and memory aspects considered. Finally, SageSched employs an uncertainty-aware scheduling policy that can yield the best overall efficiency given the request cost distributions. Testbed experiments over diverse setups confirm that SageSched can attain an efficiency improvement of over 28.7%.
